I have been farming this land for 50 years, since I was 20 years old. My mother-in-law taught me everything — I never went to school, not even one day. My father said girls don't need books, they need to know how to hold a hoe. We have 4.1 mu, just a small patch, not even half of what some families have. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, so they send money home for my grandson's school and for food. But the farm is my responsibility — I don't ask them for money for seeds or fertilizer. I have to make do with what the land gives me and what little I save from selling grain.

It is early October now, and I need to get the wheat in soon. I always plant around the 8th to the 12th, after the National Day holiday but before the cold comes. I keep some wheat seed from last year — the white kind, good for noodles — but I mix in a little new seed from Old Wang's shop. If you use your own seed too many years, the wheat gets weak and the ears get small. That costs me about 30 yuan per mu for the new seed. Before planting, I run the small rotary tiller behind Old Li's tractor — I pay him 30 yuan per mu to till the field after we cut the maize. Then I spread the fertilizer and plant by hand, row by row.

For fertilizer, I buy two big bags of that mixed fertilizer — the one with three numbers on the bag, I can't read them but Old Wang says it's good for wheat. I put about half a bag per mu before planting. That's my base. Then in spring, around Qingming, if the wheat looks yellow and sick, I topdress with urea — about half a bag per mu. Last year I did both and the wheat looked strong, so I'll do the same this year. Fertilizer is expensive now, more than last year, but if I use less I might lose half my crop. Better to eat less meat and buy the fertilizer.

Irrigating costs electricity money — about 35 to 40 yuan each time for the pump. I will irrigate three times if I can: once right after planting so the seeds wake up, once in March when the wheat comes out of winter sleep, and once when the grains are filling in late May. But if it rains well in May, I might skip that last one and save the 40 yuan. My old man is 72 now, he can't carry pipes like he used to, so I do most of the irrigation work myself. My grandson helps on weekends.

For weeds, I usually pull them by hand when I'm walking through the field. But if they look bad, I buy one small bottle of weed-killer and spray once. It's about 20 yuan per mu. I don't like using it — it smells bad and I worry about my hands — but at my age, bending down to pull weeds for 4 mu is hard.

After we harvest the wheat in early June — my son comes back for a few days to help with that — we have to plant the maize fast. Very fast. Usually within two days, three at most. If you wait too long, the maize won't have time to grow before autumn. I buy the yellow hybrid maize seed from Old Wang. It's 45 yuan per mu, which hurts, but if you plant your own seed the ears are small and the yield is bad. I put compound fertilizer in the planting holes — about half a bag per mu — and cover it up. Then if July is dry, I irrigate once when the leaves are big like trumpets, and maybe a second time if the heat is terrible. But maize is tougher than wheat. Sometimes I only irrigate once and it's fine.

For maize pests, I don't spray unless I see those green worms eating the leaves. If I see them, I buy medicine and spray. If not, I save the money. We need that money for my grandson's winter clothes.

My son and daughter-in-law work outside, so family labor is mostly me and my husband, plus my grandson on weekends. We don't hire people — we can't afford it. At harvest, my son comes back and we hire Old Li's combine for the wheat — 50 yuan per mu — but that's machine work, not hired hands. For 4.1 mu, the combine finishes in half an hour.

I expect my wheat to give about 700 to 800 jin per mu this year — that's about 350 to 400 kg if the weather is kind. For maize, I hope for 900 to 1,000 jin per mu, maybe 450 to 500 kg. If there's a drought, who knows. But I've farmed through bad years before. I'll survive this one too. I plan to spend about 1,850 yuan total on both crops this year. That's almost all my savings from last year's grain sales, but what else can I do? The land must be fed if it is to feed us.
